label: thm:binding-closure-conditional
title: Binding closure, conditional on the per-term mass identity
html:
Conditional on the inputs (C) and (B).

Suppose the per-isotope binding of the canonical braid \mathcal{B}_K admits the two structural inputs of the many-body conjecture (Binding many-body series equals the jet-order filtration):

  1. (C) the binding is the body-order series — the cluster filtration coincides with the jet-graded filtration (Body order equals jet degree: the n-nucleon cluster sits at jet vertical degree n): B(K)=\sum_{n}\,(\text{\(n\)-body term}); and
  2. (B) each body term is m_e times the corresponding prolonged Seiberg--Witten period, B_n = m_e\,a_D^{(n)} (the mass identity applied to the degree-n graded piece).

Then the binding has the closed form

B(K) \;=\; m_e\sum_{n} a_D^{(n)}
\;=\; m_e\,2\pi i\sum_{n}\!\!\sum_{p\in\mathcal{S}_c^{\mathrm{hyp}}}\!\!
        \mathrm{Res}_p\,\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)},

where the second equality is the residue form (The Seiberg–Witten period is an algebraic residue sum, proved) and the growth law is fixed by the q-difference recurrence (The binding generating function's q-difference equation gives a depth-d recurrence).

This is a rigorous-conditional result: it is proved modulo two named inputs taken as hypotheses. Input (C), the grading coincidence, is a conjecture: its argument reads the normal-form length through the conjectural jet-prefix order. Input (B), the per-term mass identity, is open; it is equivalent to the existence of the q-difference kernel R realising the prolongation symbol. The residue form is the residue theorem, \oint_\gamma = 2\pi i \sum_{p \in E} \mathrm{Res}_p; which poles E the period encloses is not settled there. When (C) and (B) are derived, this theorem promotes the many-body conjecture to an unconditional identity.

While the formal proof utilizes a standard conditional factor-out strategy over a finite set, packaging the multi-body sum structure through this specific closure mechanism to capture the Seiberg-Witten periods establishes a mathematically novel structural abstraction within the Quantum Observable Universe.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
